app.title: How the internet works
hint.zoomOut: Pinch or scroll out to go back
overview.title: Watching a video
overview.kid: Your phone asks for a video. Little parcels of data zoom through the air, down a cable and along a glass thread to the internet – and the video comes back the same way!
overview.nerd: An HTTP request leaves the phone over 802.11 Wi-Fi, is bridged onto Ethernet at the access point, NATed by the home router and forwarded over a fibre uplink to the ISP. Video segments flow back along the reverse path.
wifi.title: Radio waves
wifi.kid: The access point turns each parcel into ones and zeros and sends them through the air on an invisible radio wave. Big wiggles mean 1, small wiggles mean 0!
wifi.nerd: Bits modulate a 2.4/5/6 GHz carrier. Shown here as simple amplitude-shift keying; real Wi-Fi uses OFDM with up to 4096-QAM, packing 12 bits into every symbol on hundreds of sub-carriers.
fibre.title: Light in a glass thread
fibre.kid: Fibre is a glass thread thinner than a hair. Flashes of light bounce along inside it. Different colours can share the same thread without getting mixed up!
fibre.nerd: Light is confined to the core by total internal reflection at the core/cladding boundary. DWDM multiplexes dozens of wavelengths around 1550 nm onto one fibre, each an independent channel of 100–800 Gbit/s.
fibre.channels: Each colour is its own channel

internet.title: Inside the internet
internet.kid: The internet isn’t one big cloud. It’s a chain of boxes, each passing your parcel to the next one – from your street, through your internet company, to where the video lives.
internet.nerd: Access network (PON/OLT), an aggregation layer (L2 backhaul to the BNG), the ISP’s MPLS core, then either settlement-free peering at an IXP or paid transit, ending at a CDN cache close to you.
stop.phone.kid: Your phone wants a cat video, so it writes a little request and sends it off.
stop.phone.nerd: The app opens a TLS connection and sends an HTTP GET for the next video segment. The OS splits the data into TCP segments inside IP packets.
stop.phone-ap.kid: The request flies through the air as radio waves – no wire needed!
stop.phone-ap.nerd: 802.11ax on 5 GHz: OFDMA sub-carriers, 1024-QAM, WPA3 encryption between the phone and the AP.
stop.ap.kid: The access point catches the radio waves and sends the parcel on down a cable.
stop.ap.nerd: A layer-2 bridge: it swaps the 802.11 frame for an Ethernet frame and never reads the IP address.
stop.ap-router.kid: A copper cable carries the parcel as tiny electrical signals.
stop.ap-router.nerd: Gigabit Ethernet over four twisted pairs (1000BASE-T, PAM-5).
stop.router.kid: The router is the front door of your home. It writes your home’s address on the parcel and remembers who asked.
stop.router.nerd: NAT rewrites the private source address 192.168.1.23 to the public 203.0.113.7 and tracks the connection so replies find their way back.
stop.router-internet.kid: From your home, the parcel races along a glass thread as flashes of light.
stop.router-internet.nerd: FTTH: the ONT in your home talks XGS-PON to the OLT – 10 Gbit/s shared by the homes on one splitter.
stop.internet.kid: The internet is lots of networks holding hands. Tap it to see what’s inside!
stop.internet.nerd: ~75 000 autonomous systems exchanging routes with BGP. Tap to unfold the path through the ISP.
stop.cabinet.kid: In a box on your street, the light from lots of houses is gathered together.
stop.cabinet.nerd: A passive splitter (1:32) and the OLT line card: the first active equipment of the access network.
stop.backhaul.kid: Big switches carry the parcels from many streets towards your internet company.
stop.backhaul.nerd: L2 aggregation with Q-in-Q: an S-VLAN per cabinet and a C-VLAN per subscriber, towards the BNG.
stop.bng.kid: Here your internet company checks it’s really you and lets your parcels onto the internet.
stop.bng.nerd: The Broadband Network Gateway terminates subscriber sessions (IPoE/PPPoE), assigns addresses and applies policy and QoS.
stop.core.kid: The motorway of your internet company: super-fast connections between big cities.
stop.core.nerd: An MPLS core with 100–400G links; packets are label-switched rather than looked up at every hop.
stop.transit.kid: If there’s no shortcut, your internet company pays a bigger network to carry the parcel.
stop.transit.nerd: Paid IP transit from a tier-1 or tier-2 provider: a full routing table and reach to everything.
stop.ixp.kid: A meeting place where lots of networks swap parcels for free.
stop.ixp.nerd: An internet exchange is a big shared Ethernet fabric; networks peer over BGP, often via route servers.
stop.cdn.kid: The video lives here, in a server not far from you, so it arrives quickly.
stop.cdn.nerd: A CDN edge cache inside or next to the IXP serves the segment; only cache misses go further to the origin.
